articles.title: AI Health Company Forus Raises $150 Million at a $3 Billion Value
articles.summary: Healthcare automation startup Forus has raised $150 million at a $3 billion valuation just months after completing a previous funding round. The Series C round was led by Bain Capital Ventures, a firm that has invested in the company since its early-stage funding. Accel, Thrive Capital, General Catalyst, Redpoint Ventures, BoxGroup and Pear VC also participated in the round, Forus said Tuesday.
articles.author: Micah Barkley

articles.title: Goldman's Wheeler Says Volume of AI Debt May Pressure Spreads
articles.summary: The sheer volume of AI-related debt issuance could pressure spreads, according to Miriam Wheeler, global head of leveraged finance at Goldman Sachs. "If you look at the last couple weeks in the market on the non-IG [investment grade] side, we have seen some spread widening, particularly in the AI space," Wheeler tells Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Mistral AI Raises €3 Billion With Samsung Leading the Round
articles.summary: French artificial intelligence company Mistral AI is raising €3 billion ($3.49 billion) in a Series D funding round, with Samsung Electronics joining the round. Chief Executive Officer Arthur Mensch argues that the company is probably still undervalued and that macroeconomic reasons are starting to show that open source models will win. He speaks with Bloomberg’s Tom Mackenzie. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: At UBS, AI skills are now a condition for landing a job
articles.summary: Swiss banking giant UBS is making AI skills a required qualification from 2027 for graduates and interns in Global Banking and Markets, with applicants having to show in interviews how they use AI to improve outcomes and efficiency. Santander is already looking for advanced AI users too, while Morgan Stanley predicts more than 200,000 banking jobs in Europe will disappear within five years. The article At UBS, AI skills are now a condition for landing a job appeared first on The Decoder.

articles.title: How I stopped fearing the 3 AM pager by forcing idempotency everywhere
articles.summary: If your pipeline isn't idempotent, it isn't production-ready; it’s just a fragile script waiting to ruin your weekend. Most engineers treat "idempotency" as an academic concept for distributed systems papers, but in the trenches of fintech and healthcare, it’s the difference between a minor blip and a regulatory filing. If you can’t run your job five times in a row with the exact same input and get the exact same state, you aren't doing data engineering—you're doing data gambling. I’ve spent six years cleaning up the messes left by "append-only" thinking. I’ve seen millions of dollars in duplicate ACH transactions and patient records corrupted by "just one more retry" logic. This guide covers the patterns I use to make sure that when the scheduler kicks off at 3 AM, I can sleep through the alarm because the system knows how to fix itself. 1. articles.title: Preferred Networks CEO Eyes IPO Amid AI Chip Race
articles.summary: Japanese startup Preferred Networks is seeking to go public to mass-produce its chips, reflecting the rising cost and scale needed to stay competitive in the global AI race, CEO Daisuke Okanohara said in an interview with Bloomberg News. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Anthropic Builds Its War Chest Ahead of IPO | Bloomberg Tech 9/04/2026
articles.summary: Bloomberg’s Lisa Mateo takes a look at Anthropic as it finalizes an expansion of its revolving credit facility to $15 billion before its anticipated public filing. Plus, a look at the latest US jobs report showing the IT sector shed 23,000 jobs in August; and Apple is kicking off the John Ternus era with what could be the biggest run of new devices in its history. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Anthropic’s $15 Billion Credit Line Sets Stage for IPO
articles.summary: Anthropic’s anticipated IPO could kick off a busy fall for tech listings after SpaceX dominated the market this summer. Rainmaker Securities co-founder and Managing Director Greg Martin discusses why Anthropic’s planned $15 billion revolving credit facility strengthens its position ahead of a potential offering. He also shares how its rapid growth could support a valuation above SpaceX’s at IPO and why a successful debut could “open the floodgates” for companies including Oura, neoclouds and other long-awaited tech listings. He joins Bloomberg’s Lisa Mateo on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)
